method.summary: Four official F16 graphs {cpu, mps} x {eager, sdpa}; per row the normalized deviation sqrt(2 (1 - cosine)) from the F32 truth row; per path the envelope E = largest worst-row deviation, each graph's leave-one-out ratio over the largest other graph, and the slack s = the largest ratio rounded up to two significant digits; a Burn row passes when its deviation is at most s E (cosine at least 1 - (s E)^2 / 2) with exact top-1. Registered before any new official graph or Burn row of the round.

attempts.account: The MPS SDPA graph loaded the whole F16 model onto MPS; swap grew by 12,478 MiB in 80 s and the system volume fell from 22.6 to 11.8 GiB, and the watchdog stopped it. The CPU SDPA graph then started into that swap and was stopped 10 s later when the system volume reached 9.9 GiB. Both kills reached only /usr/bin/time: the two generators kept running until they were stopped by hand about a minute later (system volume at 5.2 GiB, recovering to 20.3 GiB as the swap files shrank); the queued control was stopped at its start gate. The driver now kills the process group, waits for 70% free memory and 15 GiB on the system volume before each graph, and reports the real exit status (attempt 1's driver.log shows exit=0 for killed runs, a $? read after a command substitution). No bundle was published by attempt 1.

decisions.what: The two-graph floor is replaced by the registered four-graph envelope rule with per-path slacks 1.1/1.1/1.1, the envelope computed in the test from authenticated rows, a fail-closed reader of the two SDPA bundles, a bundle-only re-derivation test, and every row measured before judgment. Implemented because the derivation is sound by the registered method; adopting it as the gate's rule awaits the maintainer.

awaiting_maintainer: Adopting the four-graph envelope rule for Nemotron-H: its slacks are the rounding's 1.1 over coincident worst rows, and the gate passes only because 1.0046 rounds to 1.1 (Burn's cached row 22 is 1.0231 of the envelope).

Whether a repeat of an official graph (the MPS control moves the cached envelope by about 1%), more official graphs (for example other experts implementations or a regenerated oracle on the current macOS), or pooling with other checkpoints should widen the evidence behind the slack.
